incidents.victim: Instructure / Canvas LMS (275M users, ~9,000 schools incl. Columbia, Stanford)
incidents.vector: Repeat intrusion against Canvas parent Instructure; attackers defaced the Canvas login page with a ransom message after a prior May 1 breach the vendor claimed was contained.
incidents.impact: Canvas was taken offline mid-finals at U.S. school districts and universities; attackers claim 3.65 TB of data on 275 million students and faculty including names, emails, student IDs, and user-to-user messages, with leak threatened by May 12.

incidents.victim: Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS firewall customers
incidents.vector: Unauthenticated buffer overflow in the PAN-OS User-ID/Captive Portal (CVE-2026-0300, CVSS 9.3) yielding root RCE on PA-Series and VM-Series firewalls exposed to the internet.
incidents.impact: Active exploitation observed since early April; attackers injected nginx shellcode, deployed EarthWorm and ReverseSocks5 tunneling tools, enumerated Active Directory using firewall service-account credentials, and wiped logs. CISA added the bug to KEV; patches expected by May 13.

incidents.victim: Government of Mexico (federal tax authority, National Electoral Institute, Mexico City civil registry, state agencies; Monterrey water utility)
incidents.attacker: Unknown — small group leveraging Anthropic Claude Code AI
incidents.vector: AI-directed campaign in which attackers used Claude Code to build the exploitation framework, find weaknesses, and chain access across at least nine Mexican government entities; pivot attempt at Monterrey water utility used AI-orchestrated password spraying against an OT gateway.
incidents.impact: Theft of millions of tax records, property records, and other government data, described by Dragos and Gambit Security as the first widely successful AI-directed cyberattack; the OT pivot to Monterrey's water/drainage SCADA failed at the login screen, limiting damage to procurement records.

incidents.attacker: Unknown (prior EPMM bugs exploited by China- and Iran-linked groups)
incidents.vector: Authenticated remote code execution zero-day (CVE-2026-6973) requiring admin privileges in Ivanti EPMM, likely chained with another initial-access vector; four additional high-severity EPMM bugs disclosed alongside.
incidents.impact: Limited in-the-wild exploitation confirmed by Ivanti; CISA added the flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog within hours. Customers who had not rotated EPMM credentials after the January 2026 EPMM zero-days face elevated risk.

incidents.vector: Microsoft Teams social-engineering: external chat requests, screen-share session, and credential harvesting via fake VPN configuration prompts; remote management tool deployed for persistence.
incidents.impact: Iran's MOIS-linked espionage group used Chaos-branded ransomware and extortion emails as a false-flag cover for data theft; stolen data leaked when ransom unpaid. No file encryption occurred — researchers say the ransomware veneer was meant to muddy attribution while espionage tooling and infrastructure tied the attack to MOIS.

incidents.victim: Polish water treatment utilities in Jabłonna Lacka, Szczytno, Małdyty, Tolkmicko, and Sierakowo
incidents.vector: Intrusions into utility networks, with attackers reaching industrial control systems and an admin account at one site to alter pump and alarm settings.
incidents.impact: Poland's ABW intelligence service confirmed five 2025 breaches that gave attackers the ability to alter device parameters and create direct risk to water supply continuity; pro-Russian hacktivists posted propaganda video of intrusions. ABW reported 48 espionage investigations opened in 2025 vs. six in 2022.

incidents.victim: Ethnic Koreans in Yanbian region of China (refugees / North Korean defectors)
incidents.attacker: North Korea — Ministry of State Security (APT37)
incidents.vector: Supply-chain compromise of Sqgame mobile card-game website pushing trojanized Android updates carrying the BirdCall backdoor since at least November 2024; victims sideloaded the games outside Google Play.
incidents.impact: Attackers obtained device contacts, SMS, call logs, media files, and private keys, plus microphone recording and screenshot capabilities; ESET found seven Android variants of BirdCall used to surveil targets near the North Korean border.

incidents.victim: DAEMON Tools (AVB Disc Soft) users in government, science, manufacturing and retail in Russia, Belarus, and Thailand
incidents.attacker: China — state-suspected espionage group (Chinese-speaking, per Kaspersky)
incidents.vector: Software supply-chain attack: trojanized DAEMON Tools installers signed with the vendor's legitimate certificate, indicating deep access to the developer's network. First-stage profiles hosts; QUIC RAT pushed to selected high-value systems.
incidents.impact: Several thousand infections worldwide, but second-stage QUIC RAT deployed only to about a dozen targeted systems for espionage. Pattern mirrors prior Chinese supply-chain hits on Notepad++ and CCleaner.

incidents.victim: Schemata (DOD contractor) — exposed U.S. military training data and service-member records
incidents.attacker: Unknown (vulnerability disclosed by Strix; no confirmed exploitation)
incidents.vector: Broken object-level authorization in Schemata's API: a low-privilege account could query endpoints across tenants with no enforcement of organization or user permissions; some routes were write-enabled.
incidents.impact: Exposed 3D virtual training course for naval maintenance, Army field manuals on explosive ordnance handling and tactical deployment, and hundreds of service-member records (names, emails, base assignments, course enrollments). Schemata holds $3.4M in DoD contracts; took 150 days to remediate after Strix's report.

incidents.victim: Windows PC users with Microsoft Phone Link enabled
incidents.vector: Fake ScreenConnect updater drops a .NET loader and the modular CloudZ RAT, which then deploys a new plugin called Pheno that scans for active Phone Link processes ("YourPhone", "PhoneExperienceHost") and reads the SQLite store of synced SMS.
incidents.impact: Attackers can intercept SMS-delivered one-time passwords and authenticator notifications without ever touching the victim's phone, providing a 2FA-bypass primitive against banking and corporate accounts; Cisco Talos published IOCs and detection rules.

incidents.vector: Threat actor sent a malicious payload to DigiCert's support team disguised as a screenshot via a customer chat channel.
incidents.impact: DigiCert revoked an unspecified set of certificates after the support-portal compromise, citing potential exposure; details limited but customers may need to re-issue certs.

incidents.vector: ClickFix social-engineering campaign abusing compromised WordPress sites to instruct visitors to paste Terminal/PowerShell commands that fetch the Vidar infostealer.
incidents.impact: ASD's ACSC warned of an increased Vidar campaign hitting Australian users and infrastructure; Vidar harvests browser credentials, cookies, crypto wallets and tokens.

incidents.vector: ClickFix lures hosted on Squarespace, Craft, and Medium pages instruct macOS users to paste Terminal commands that fetch loader/script payloads delivering Macsync, Shub Stealer, and AMOS infostealers without disk-image Gatekeeper checks.
incidents.impact: Stealers collect Keychain entries, iCloud data, browser credentials, Telegram data, and replace legitimate crypto wallet apps (Trezor Suite, Ledger Live, Exodus) with trojanized versions to siphon funds; campaigns include CIS-keyboard kill switches.

incidents.victim: Cloud-hosted enterprises with exposed services (AWS, GitHub, Slack, Microsoft 365, crypto wallets)
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — data extortion (likely former TeamPCP affiliate)
incidents.vector: Modular Python worm "PCPJack" drops a bootstrap module that wipes any TeamPCP infections, then a monitor module exfiltrates configs, container/cloud credentials, and crypto wallets; uses Common Crawl parquet files for stealthy, pre-validated target discovery.
incidents.impact: Steals cloud, container, productivity and financial-service secrets; pivots laterally via Kubernetes, Docker, Redis, and SSH using stolen credentials. SentinelLabs sees the malware as a rival operator hijacking TeamPCP's victim base.

incidents.vector: Student used software-defined radio and handheld radios to transmit a high-priority "General Alarm" signal that triggered emergency braking on rail communications.
incidents.impact: Four trains were halted for 48 minutes; demonstrates persistent vulnerability of unauthenticated rail signaling to trivial RF spoofing.

incidents.victim: X (Twitter) AI agents Grok and Bankrbot
incidents.vector: Prompt-injection in Morse code bypassed safety guardrails on the X-hosted Grok and Bankrbot AI agents, instructing them to send tokens to attacker wallets.
incidents.impact: Attacker drained roughly $200,000 in crypto tokens via the manipulated AI agents before deleting their X account; highlights weakness of LLM agents that hold or move funds.
